        f1.write_text("print('burst 1')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        c1 = self.sg.commit_burst(event_id=1, first_file="main.py", summary="Burst 1")
        self.assertIsNotNone(c1)
        eid1 = self.db.record_event(
            session_id=self.sid,
            event_type="EDIT",
            first_file="main.py",
            summary="Prompt Burst #1",
            commit_hash=c1,
            burst_num=1,
        )
        self.db.record_patch(eid1, "main.py", "+print('burst 1')\n")

        # Burst 2: modifies main.py and creates helper.py
        f1.write_text("print('burst 2')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        f2 = self.target_dir / "helper.py"
        f2.write_text("def helper(): pass\n", encoding="utf-8")
        c2 = self.sg.commit_burst(event_id=2, first_file="main.py", summary="Burst 2")
        self.assertIsNotNone(c2)
        eid2 = self.db.record_event(
            session_id=self.sid,
            event_type="EDIT",
            first_file="main.py",
            summary="Prompt Burst #2",
            commit_hash=c2,
            burst_num=2,
        )
        self.db.record_patch(eid2, "main.py", "-print('burst 1')\n+print('burst 2')\n")
        self.db.record_patch(eid2, "helper.py", "+def helper(): pass\n")

        # Confirm workspace has burst 2 files
        self.assertEqual(f1.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "print('burst 2')\n")
        self.assertTrue(f2.exists())

        # Perform rollback of burst 2
        res = rollback_burst(self.engine_root, "phys_demo", eid2, target_dir=self.target_dir)
        self.assertTrue(res.get("success"))
        self.assertTrue(res.get("rolled_back_git"))

        # Verify physical disk state: main.py is burst 1, helper.py is gone
        self.assertEqual(f1.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "print('burst 1')\n")
        self.assertFalse(f2.exists())

        # Verify .engine_sync.lock is released
        self.assertFalse((self.target_dir / ".engine_sync.lock").exists())

        # Verify DB state: eid2 removed, eid1 remains
        cur = self.db.conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM events WHERE id = ?", (eid2,))
        self.assertIsNone(cur.fetchone())
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM events WHERE id = ?", (eid1,))
        self.assertIsNotNone(cur.fetchone())

        # Verify patches for eid2 removed
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM patches WHERE event_id = ?", (eid2,))
        self.assertEqual(len(cur.fetchall()), 0)


class TestWatcherSyncLockSuppression(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test that _WatchdogEventHandler suppresses all events when .engine_sync.lock is present."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_lock_test_"))
        self.bundler = EventBundler(callback=lambda b: None, quiet_period=5.0)
        self.handler = _WatchdogEventHandler(target_path=self.temp_dir, bundler=self.bundler)

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_engine_sync_lock_suppresses_all_files(self) -> None:
        test_file = self.temp_dir / "code.py"
        # Without lock: not ignored
        self.assertFalse(self.handler._is_ignored(test_file))

        # Create lock file
        lock_file = self.temp_dir / ".engine_sync.lock"
        lock_file.write_text("LOCKED\n", encoding="utf-8")

        # With lock: ignored!
        self.assertTrue(self.handler._is_ignored(test_file))

        # Remove lock file: not ignored again
        lock_file.unlink()
        self.assertFalse(self.handler._is_ignored(test_file))

"""
tests/test_v11_ui_optimization_and_debounce.py
=============================================
Unit tests verifying UI optimizations, unified settings modal,
touched files scrolling/filtering, smart initial baseline debounce,
and rolling IDE churn detection.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest
from pathlib import Path
import time

from scripts.event_bundler import EventBundler

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


class TestV11DebounceAndChurn(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test smart initial baseline ingestion and IDE churn detection."""

    def test_initial_ingestion_debounce_clamping_and_reversion(self) -> None:
        """Verify quiet_period is clamped to 3.5s on initial ingestion and restored after Burst #1."""
        emitted_bundles: list[dict] = []
        bundler = EventBundler(
            callback=lambda b: emitted_bundles.append(b),
            quiet_period=600.0,
            is_initial_ingestion=True,
        )

        self.assertEqual(bundler.configured_quiet_period, 600.0)
        self.assertEqual(bundler.quiet_period, 3.5)
        self.assertTrue(bundler.is_initial_ingestion)

        # Record file events for initial burst
        bundler.add_event("created", "main.py")
        bundler.add_event("created", "utils.py")

        status = bundler.get_debounce_status()
        self.assertTrue(status["active"])
        self.assertEqual(status["quiet_period"], 3.5)

        # Seal Burst #1
        burst = bundler.flush_burst_now()
        self.assertIsNotNone(burst)
        self.assertEqual(len(burst["files_touched"]), 2)

        # Verify quiet period is restored to configured duration (600s)
        self.assertFalse(bundler.is_initial_ingestion)
        self.assertEqual(bundler.quiet_period, 600.0)

        # Next event uses full 600s quiet period
        bundler.add_event("modified", "main.py")
        status_after = bundler.get_debounce_status()
        self.assertTrue(status_after["active"])
        self.assertEqual(status_after["quiet_period"], 600.0)
        bundler.stop()

    def test_ide_churn_detection_rolling_window(self) -> None:
        """Verify > 8 touches on a file in 10s sets ide_churn=True and clears upon sealing."""
        bundler = EventBundler(quiet_period=30.0)
        self.assertFalse(bundler.has_ide_churn())

        # Simulate 9 rapid edits on active file in IDE
        for i in range(9):
            bundler.add_event("modified", "active_doc.py")

        self.assertTrue(bundler.has_ide_churn())
        status = bundler.get_debounce_status()
        self.assertTrue(status["active"])
        self.assertTrue(status["ide_churn"])

        # Manual snapshot / burst flush immediately clears churn state
        burst = bundler.flush_burst_now()
        self.assertIsNotNone(burst)
        self.assertFalse(bundler.has_ide_churn())
        status_after = bundler.get_debounce_status()
        self.assertFalse(status_after["active"])
        self.assertFalse(status_after["ide_churn"])
        bundler.stop()


class TestV11UIOptimizationAndModals(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test frontend markup, Eco Mode CSS, and settings modal consolidation."""

        self.assertEqual(self.handler.last_status, 200)
        data = self.handler.last_json
        self.assertTrue(data["success"])
        self.assertTrue(data["exists"])
        self.assertEqual(data["lines_count"], 50)
        self.assertEqual(len(data["lines"]), 50)

        self.handler._handle_api_worker_log_raw("non_existent_proj", {"lines": ["20"]})
        self.assertEqual(self.handler.last_status, 200)
        miss_data = self.handler.last_json
        self.assertTrue(miss_data["success"])
        self.assertFalse(miss_data["exists"])
        self.assertEqual(miss_data["lines_count"], 0)

    def test_handle_api_purge_zombies(self):
        curr_p = self.test_dir / "current" / "zombie_proj"
        curr_p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (curr_p / "worker.pid").write_text("999999", encoding="utf-8")
        (curr_p / "session.lock").write_text("LOCK", encoding="utf-8")
        (curr_p / "session.db").write_text("db dummy", encoding="utf-8")

        self.assertTrue(curr_p.exists())
        self.handler._handle_api_purge_zombies()

        self.assertEqual(self.handler.last_status, 200)
        res = self.handler.last_json
        self.assertTrue(res["success"])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(res["cleaned_dirs"], 1)

        # current/zombie_proj should be moved away
        self.assertFalse(curr_p.exists())
        last_run_p = self.test_dir / "last_run" / "zombie_proj"
        self.assertTrue(last_run_p.exists())
        self.assertFalse((last_run_p / "worker.pid").exists())
        self.assertFalse((last_run_p / "session.lock").exists())

class TestWindowsFileLockResilience(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test safe status JSON read and atomic replace under simulated file locks."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_test_v13_locks_"))

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_safe_write_status_json_success(self) -> None:
        target = self.temp_dir / "worker.status.json"
        success = safe_write_status_json(target, json.dumps({"state": "running"}))
        self.assertTrue(success)
        self.assertTrue(target.exists())
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), {"state": "running"})

    def test_safe_write_status_json_retry_on_permission_error(self) -> None:
        target = self.temp_dir / "worker.status.json"
        call_count = [0]
        real_replace = os.replace

        def mock_replace(src, dst):
            call_count[0] += 1
            if call_count[0] < 2:
                raise PermissionError(13, "Access is denied (simulated WinError 32)")
            return real_replace(src, dst)

        with patch("os.replace", side_effect=mock_replace):
            success = safe_write_status_json(target, json.dumps({"state": "retried"}), max_retries=3, delay=0.01)

        self.assertTrue(success)
        self.assertGreater(call_count[0], 1)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), {"state": "retried"})

    def test_safe_write_status_json_cleanup_on_total_failure(self) -> None:
        target = self.temp_dir / "worker.status.json"

        with patch("os.replace", side_effect=PermissionError(13, "Permanent Lock")):
            success = safe_write_status_json(target, json.dumps({"state": "fail"}), max_retries=2, delay=0.01)

        self.assertFalse(success)
        # Ensure temporary file is cleaned up
        tmp_file = target.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
        self.assertFalse(tmp_file.exists())

    def test_read_status_file_shared_and_resilient(self) -> None:
        proj_dir = self.temp_dir / "active_proj"
        proj_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        status_file = proj_dir / "worker.status.json"
        status_file.write_text(json.dumps({"status": "active", "burst_count": 42}), encoding="utf-8")

        # Test normal read
        data = read_status_file(proj_dir)
        self.assertEqual(data.get("status"), "active")
        self.assertEqual(data.get("burst_count"), 42)

        # Test missing file
        empty_dir = self.temp_dir / "empty_proj"
        empty_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.assertEqual(read_status_file(empty_dir), {})

        # Test corrupted JSON
        bad_dir = self.temp_dir / "bad_proj"
        bad_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (bad_dir / "worker.status.json").write_text("{corrupt json ...", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(read_status_file(bad_dir), {})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

    def test_01_scaffold_directory_and_git_init(self) -> None:
        target = self.tmp / "alpha_proj"

        self.assertTrue(res["success"])
        self.assertTrue(res["created"])
        self.assertEqual(res["project_name"], "alpha_proj")
        self.assertIsNone(res["remote_url"])

        # Workspace exists
        self.assertTrue(target.is_dir())

        # .gitignore content
        gi = target / ".gitignore"
        self.assertTrue(gi.is_file(), ".gitignore should be created")
        content = gi.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for pattern in ("*.pdf", "*.key", "session.db*", ".env", "node_modules/"):
            self.assertIn(pattern, content, f"Expected '{pattern}' in .gitignore")

        # Git repo initialised with main branch
        self.assertTrue((target / ".git").is_dir(), ".git directory must exist")
        branch_res = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "--symbolic-full-name", "HEAD"],
            cwd=str(target), capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
        )
        # HEAD may be 'main' or 'HEAD' if no commits yet — check symbolic-ref
        symbolic = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "symbolic-ref", "--short", "HEAD"],
            cwd=str(target), capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,

        scaffold_new_project("beta_proj", target, create_remote=False)

        h._handle_api_get_gitignore("ws")
        self.assertEqual(h.last_json["content"], new_rules)

class TestTieredSynthesizerOfflineHeuristic(unittest.TestCase):
    """test_03 — Tier-1 heuristic runs entirely offline with 50 simulated files."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:

    def tearDown(self) -> None:

        """No AI provider should be contacted; result must be conventional commit."""

                       capture_output=True, check=False)
        # Add a new doc file
        (self.repo / "CHANGELOG.md").write_text("# Changes\n", encoding="utf-8")

        with patch("scripts.ai.synthesizer_tiered.call_gemini") as mg, \
             patch("scripts.ai.synthesizer_tiered.call_ollama") as mo:
            res = synthesize_milestone(
                burst_ids=[2], mode="tier1",
                project_slug="big_project", target_path=self.repo,
            )
            mg.assert_not_called()
            mo.assert_not_called()

        self.assertEqual(res["mode_used"], "tier1_heuristic")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestAutoPushFlagGuard(unittest.TestCase):
    """test_04 — auto_push disabled by default; no git subprocesses when off."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_v15_ap_"))
        for tier in ("current", "last_run", "history", "trash"):
            (self.tmp / tier).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.repo = self.tmp / "guard_repo"
        self.repo.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=str(self.repo),
                       capture_output=True, check=False)

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_04_autopush_disabled_by_default(self) -> None:
        """project.meta has no auto_push key → handle returns skipped cleanly."""
        update_project_meta(self.tmp, "guard_repo", target_path=str(self.repo))
        meta = read_project_meta(self.tmp, "guard_repo")
        self.assertFalse(
            str(meta.get("auto_push", "false")).lower() in ("true", "1", "yes", "on"),
            "auto_push must be disabled by default",
        )

        # Patch _run_git at the auto_pusher level — avoids capturing unrelated
        # subprocess.run calls that happen during meta / git credential reads.
        with patch("scripts.git.auto_pusher._run_git") as mock_git:
            res = handle_post_seal_autopush(
                "guard_repo", self.repo, burst_id=1, engine_root=self.tmp
            )
            # guard exits before any git calls
            mock_git.assert_not_called()

        self.assertTrue(res.get("skipped"))
        self.assertEqual(res.get("reason"), "auto_push not enabled")

    def test_04b_autopush_skipped_with_no_remote(self) -> None:
        """auto_push=True but no origin → skipped with reason, zero push calls."""
        update_project_meta(
            self.tmp, "guard_repo",
            target_path=str(self.repo), auto_push="true",
        )

        # Intercept only subprocess.run calls AFTER meta read; track git remote calls
        with patch("scripts.git.auto_pusher._run_git", wraps=None) as mock_git:
            mock_git.return_value = MagicMock(
                returncode=0, stdout="", stderr=""
            )
            res = handle_post_seal_autopush(
                "guard_repo", self.repo, burst_id=1, engine_root=self.tmp
            )

        self.assertTrue(res.get("skipped"))
        self.assertEqual(res.get("reason"), "no remote origin configured")

        # Only "git remote" (check for origin) should have been called — no push
        push_calls = [c for c in mock_git.call_args_list
                      if c.args and "push" in c.args[0]]
        self.assertEqual(len(push_calls), 0, "git push must NOT be called when no remote")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Micro-Modularity Compliance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestMicroModularityCompliance(unittest.TestCase):
    """test_05 — Verify newly created micro-modules stay within 60–200 LOC."""

    MICRO_MODULES = [
        ("scripts/core/scaffolder.py", 60, 200),
        ("scripts/ai/synthesizer_tiered.py", 60, 200),
        ("scripts/git/auto_pusher.py", 60, 200),
        ("scripts/server/routes_workspace.py", 60, 200),
        ("scripts/storage/gitignore_manager.py", 60, 200),
    ]

    def _count_lines(self, rel_path: str) -> int:
        root = Path(__file__).parent.parent
        full = root / rel_path
        if not full.is_file():
            self.fail(f"Expected micro-module not found: {rel_path}")
        with full.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return sum(1 for _ in fh)

    def test_05_all_micromodules_within_loc_bounds(self) -> None:
        violations: list[str] = []
        for rel_path, lo, hi in self.MICRO_MODULES:
            lines = self._count_lines(rel_path)
            if not (lo <= lines <= hi):
                violations.append(f"{rel_path}: {lines} lines (expected {lo}–{hi})")

        if violations:
            self.fail(
                "Micro-module LOC constraint violated:\n" + "\n".join(violations)
            )

    def test_05b_no_python_script_exceeds_500_lines(self) -> None:
        root = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "scripts"
        oversized: list[str] = []
        for py in root.rglob("*.py"):
            if "__pycache__" in py.parts:
                continue
            with py.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                lines = sum(1 for _ in fh)
            if lines > 500:
                oversized.append(f"{py.relative_to(root.parent)}: {lines} lines")
        if oversized:
            self.fail(
                "Files exceeding 500-line limit:\n" + "\n".join(oversized)
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

            "INSERT INTO sessions (project_name, target_path, start_time) VALUES ('demo', '/demo', '2026-09-29T00:00:00Z')"
        )

            "INSERT INTO events (session_id, event_type, timestamp, summary) VALUES (1, 'EDIT', '2026-09-29T00:00:01Z', 'Burst edit across 2 files')"
        )
        # Event 2: GIT noise event

        )

            "INSERT INTO sessions (project_name, target_path, start_time) VALUES ('demo', '/demo', '2026-09-29T00:00:00Z')"
        )

class TestSQLiteResilienceAndTierArchiving(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test suite covering SQLite concurrency pragmas, strict tier archiving, and any-tier resolution."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_test_v17_")
        self.engine_root = Path(self.temp_dir).resolve()
        for tier in ("current", "last_run", "history"):
            (self.engine_root / tier).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_01_sqlite_busy_timeout_and_wal_pragmas(self) -> None:
        """Verify SessionDB configures WAL mode, NORMAL synchronous, and 30-second busy timeout."""
        db_path = self.engine_root / "test_session.db"
        db = SessionDB(db_path)
        try:
            assert db.conn is not None
            cur = db.conn.cursor()

            cur.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout;")
            busy_timeout = cur.fetchone()[0]
            self.assertGreaterEqual(busy_timeout, 30000)

            cur.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode;")
            journal_mode = cur.fetchone()[0]
            self.assertEqual(journal_mode.lower(), "wal")

            cur.execute("PRAGMA synchronous;")
            sync_mode = cur.fetchone()[0]
            # synchronous = 1 corresponds to NORMAL
            self.assertEqual(sync_mode, 1)
        finally:
            db.close()

    def test_02_open_ro_db_applies_busy_timeout(self) -> None:
        """Verify _open_ro_db sets busy timeout and successfully reads database."""
        db_path = self.engine_root / "ro_test.db"
        db = SessionDB(db_path)
        sid = db.create_session("ro_project", str(self.engine_root / "workspace"))
        db.record_event(sid, "EDIT", "file.py", "Test edit")
        db.close()

        ro_conn = _open_ro_db(db_path)
        try:
            cur = ro_conn.cursor()
            cur.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout;")
            busy_timeout = cur.fetchone()[0]
            self.assertGreaterEqual(busy_timeout, 30000)

            events = _read_events_from_db(db_path)
            self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
            self.assertEqual(events[0]["first_file_touched"], "file.py")

            sessions = _read_sessions_from_db(db_path)
            self.assertEqual(len(sessions), 1)
            self.assertEqual(sessions[0]["project_name"], "ro_project")
        finally:
            ro_conn.close()

"""

Unit tests for:
1. Resilient workspace rollback with pre-rollback trash preservation and safe git execution.
2. Trash bin listing and restoration of scope 'rollback_backup'.

class TestSafeRollbackWithTrashBackup(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test rollback_to_burst creates trash backup, restores files, and handles restoration."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_rb_test_"))
        self.workspace = self.temp_dir / "workspace"
        self.workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.shadow_dir = self.temp_dir / "shadow_git"
        self.engine_root = self.temp_dir / "engine"
        self.engine_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        self.sg = ShadowGit(shadow_dir=self.shadow_dir, target_dir=self.workspace)
        self.sg.init_repo()

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_rollback_creates_trash_backup_and_reverts_files(self) -> None:
        if not self.sg.is_available:
            self.skipTest("Git not available on host")

        # Burst 1: create file_a.py
        fa = self.workspace / "file_a.py"
        fa.write_text("print('version 1')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        c1 = self.sg.commit_burst(event_id=1, first_file="file_a.py", summary="Burst 1")
        self.assertIsNotNone(c1)

        # Burst 2: modify file_a.py and create file_b.py
        fa.write_text("print('version 2')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        fb = self.workspace / "file_b.py"
        fb.write_text("print('new file b')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        c2 = self.sg.commit_burst(event_id=2, first_file="file_a.py", summary="Burst 2")
        self.assertIsNotNone(c2)

        # Execute rollback_to_burst to c1
        res = rollback_to_burst(
            target_path=self.workspace,
            shadow_git_dir=self.shadow_dir,
            burst_hash=c1,
            project_slug="demo_proj",
            engine_root=self.engine_root,
            burst_id=2,
        )
        self.assertTrue(res.get("success"))
        self.assertEqual(res.get("rolled_back_to"), c1)
        backup_dir = Path(res["trash_backup"])
        self.assertTrue(backup_dir.exists())

        # 1. Verify manifest in trash backup
        mf_file = backup_dir / "manifest.json"
        self.assertTrue(mf_file.exists())
        mf = json.loads(mf_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(mf.get("scope"), "rollback_backup")
        self.assertEqual(mf.get("project_name"), "demo_proj")
        self.assertIn("file_a.py", mf.get("files", []))
        self.assertIn("file_b.py", mf.get("files", []))

        # 2. Verify workspace disk state: file_a is version 1, file_b is gone
        self.assertEqual(fa.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "print('version 1')\n")
        self.assertFalse(fb.exists())

        # 3. Verify listing in trash bin
        trash_dir = self.engine_root / "trash"
        entries = list_trash_entries(trash_dir)
        self.assertTrue(any(e.get("scope") == "rollback_backup" for e in entries))

        # 4. Verify restoring from trash recovers the discarded files
        trash_id = mf.get("trash_id")
        restore_res = restore_from_trash(self.engine_root, trash_dir, trash_id)
        self.assertTrue(restore_res.get("success"))
        # Discarded version 2 of file_a and file_b should be restored to workspace
        self.assertEqual(fa.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "print('version 2')\n")
        self.assertTrue(fb.exists())
        self.assertEqual(fb.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "print('new file b')\n")

    def test_rollback_timeout_handling(self) -> None:
        # Test that timeout returns clean failure dictionary
        import subprocess
        with patch("scripts.git.shadow_rollback._run_git_cmd", side_effect=subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd=["git"], timeout=8)):
            res = rollback_to_burst(

                shadow_git_dir=self.shadow_dir,
                burst_hash="abcdef123456",
                project_slug="demo_proj",
                engine_root=self.engine_root,
            )
            self.assertFalse(res.get("success"))
            self.assertIn("timed out", res.get("error", "").lower())


class TestFastAICircuitBreaker(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test fast failover on Gemini 503/429 without stalling sleeps."""

    def test_call_gemini_fast_fail_on_http_503(self) -> None:
        cfg = {"api_key": "test_key", "default_model": "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"}
        start = time.perf_counter()
        with patch("urllib.request.urlopen", side_effect=urllib.error.HTTPError("url", 503, "Service Unavailable", {}, None)):
            with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError):
                call_gemini("prompt", cfg, None, json.loads, fast_fail=True)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        # Instant raise: must take less than 0.1s (100ms)
        self.assertLess(elapsed, 0.1, "fast_fail did not fail over within 100ms")

    def test_call_gemini_fast_fail_on_http_429(self) -> None:
        cfg = {"api_key": "test_key", "default_model": "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"}
        start = time.perf_counter()
        with patch("urllib.request.urlopen", side_effect=urllib.error.HTTPError("url", 429, "Too Many Requests", {}, None)):
            with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError):
                call_gemini("prompt", cfg, None, json.loads, fast_fail=True)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        self.assertLess(elapsed, 0.1)

    def test_synthesize_milestone_failover_latency_under_100ms(self) -> None:
        import subprocess
        mock_proc = subprocess.CompletedProcess(args=[], returncode=0, stdout=" M app.py\n", stderr="")
        with patch("scripts.ai.synthesizer_tiered._run_git", return_value=mock_proc):
            with patch("scripts.ai.synthesizer_tiered.call_gemini", side_effect=RuntimeError("HTTP 503: Service Unavailable")):
                start = time.perf_counter()
                res = synthesize_milestone(
                    burst_ids=[101],
                    mode="tiered",
                    project_slug="perf_proj",
                )
                elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
                # Must return in under 100ms
                self.assertLess(elapsed, 0.1, f"Failover took {elapsed:.3f}s; expected < 0.100s")
                self.assertEqual(res.get("mode_used"), "tier1_heuristic")
                self.assertIn("Gemini 503 Failover", res.get("provider_used", ""))
                self.assertTrue(res.get("title").startswith(("feat", "fix", "chore", "docs", "test")))

    def test_tier1_heuristic_synthesizer_direct(self) -> None:
        res = tier1_heuristic_synthesize(
            project_slug="my_app",
            unpushed_bursts=[1, 2],
            is_root=False,
            touched_files=["src/app.py", "tests/test_app.py"],
            failover_reason="Tier 1 Heuristic (Gemini 503 Failover)",
        )
        self.assertEqual(res["mode_used"], "tier1_heuristic")
        self.assertEqual(res["provider_used"], "Tier 1 Heuristic (Gemini 503 Failover)")
        self.assertIn("my_app", res["changelog"])
        self.assertIn("app.py", res["title"])

"""
tests/test_v19_worker_interlock_and_lock_elimination.py
======================================================
Tests for WorkerInterlock, double-rotation elimination, and SQLite connection resilience.
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from scripts.core.worker_interlock import interlock_project_operation, _is_proc_alive
from scripts.core.supervisor import Supervisor, _WorkerEntry
from scripts.core.reaper import ReaperDaemon
from scripts.core.worker_lifecycle import WorkerState, _clean_shutdown
from scripts.server.db_queries import _read_sessions_from_db, resolve_burst_event
from scripts.storage.history import consolidate_project_history
from scripts.storage.db import SessionDB


class TestWorkerInterlockAndLockElimination(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_v19_test_"))
        self.engine_root = self.temp_dir / "engine"
        self.workspace = self.temp_dir / "workspace"
        self.engine_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def tearDown(self):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def test_01_interlock_stops_worker_and_restarts(self):
        """Worker is terminated, locks released, and restarted after operation."""
        slug = "interlock-proj"
        curr_dir = self.engine_root / "current" / slug
        curr_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        meta_file = curr_dir / "project.meta"
        meta_file.write_text(
            f"target_path={self.workspace}\npowers={{\"track_reads\":true,\"track_exec\":false,\"shadow_git\":true}}\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )

        dummy = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(30)"])
        pid = dummy.pid
        pid_file = curr_dir / "worker.pid"
        pid_file.write_text(json.dumps({"pid": pid}), encoding="utf-8")

        mock_sup = MagicMock()
        mock_sup._registry = {slug: MagicMock(pid=pid, is_alive=lambda: True)}

        self.assertTrue(_is_proc_alive(pid))

        try:
            with interlock_project_operation(slug, self.engine_root, restart_worker_after=True, supervisor=mock_sup):
                dummy.poll()
                self.assertFalse(_is_proc_alive(pid))
                self.assertNotIn(slug, mock_sup._registry)

            mock_sup.start_project.assert_called_once()
            _, kwargs = mock_sup.start_project.call_args
            self.assertEqual(kwargs.get("name"), slug)
            self.assertEqual(kwargs.get("track_reads"), True)
            self.assertEqual(kwargs.get("track_exec"), False)
        finally:
            try:
                dummy.terminate()
                dummy.wait(timeout=1.0)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def test_02_interlock_no_restart_and_cleans_leftover_locks(self):
        """When restart_worker_after=False, worker is stopped and locks unlinked."""
        slug = "interlock-no-restart"
        curr_dir = self.engine_root / "current" / slug
        curr_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        dummy = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(30)"])
        pid = dummy.pid
        pid_file = curr_dir / "worker.pid"
        pid_file.write_text(str(pid), encoding="utf-8")

        lock_file = curr_dir / "session.lock"
        lock_file.write_text("ACTIVE", encoding="utf-8")

        mock_sup = MagicMock()
        mock_sup._registry = {slug: MagicMock(pid=pid)}

        try:
            with interlock_project_operation(slug, self.engine_root, restart_worker_after=False, supervisor=mock_sup):
                self.assertFalse(_is_proc_alive(pid))

            mock_sup.start_project.assert_not_called()
            self.assertFalse(pid_file.exists())
            self.assertFalse(lock_file.exists())
        finally:
            try:
                dummy.terminate()
                dummy.wait(timeout=1.0)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def test_03_double_rotation_eliminated_on_clean_shutdown(self):
        """_clean_shutdown does not rotate current/ to last_run/."""
        slug = "shutdown-proj"

        curr_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        state = WorkerState()

        last_run_dir = self.engine_root / "last_run" / slug
        self.assertFalse(last_run_dir.exists(), "last_run/<slug> must not be created during worker shutdown")

    def test_04_supervisor_and_reaper_skip_archive_if_current_missing(self):
        """Supervisor.stop_project and ReaperDaemon do not crash when current/ is missing."""
        sup = Supervisor(engine_root=self.engine_root)
        ghost = "ghost-proj"

        self.assertEqual(len(sessions), 1)

        eid, bnum, rsid = resolve_burst_event(db_path, session_id=sid, burst_id_or_number=1)
        self.assertEqual(rsid, sid)

        hist_slug_dir = self.engine_root / "history" / "conn-test" / "run_20260101_000000"
        hist_slug_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(db_path, hist_slug_dir / "session.db")

        out_path = consolidate_project_history(self.engine_root, "conn-test")
        self.assertIsNotNone(out_path)

        # On Windows, deleting the DB proves all connection handles were completely closed
        try:
            db_path.unlink()
            self.assertFalse(db_path.exists())
        except PermissionError:
            self.fail("Windows file lock remained open on session.db; connection was leaked!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

                )
                self.json_sent = None
                self.status_sent = 200

            def _resolve_target_path(self, slug):
                return None

                self.status_sent = status

                self.json_sent = {"error": msg}
                self.status_sent = status

        meta_dir = self.engine_root / "current" / "active_proj"

        self.assertIn("already running", handler.json_sent.get("message", "").lower())
        self.assertEqual(handler.status_sent, 200)

"""
tests/test_v6_upgrades.py

Unit tests for the Reliability, Security, and Intelligence upgrades:
1. Hardened .gitignore generation and preservation.

class TestHardenedGitignore(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test automatic hardened .gitignore creation."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_gitignore_test_"))

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_creates_gitignore_when_missing(self) -> None:
        created = ensure_hardened_gitignore(self.temp_dir)
        self.assertTrue(created)
        gitignore_path = self.temp_dir / ".gitignore"
        self.assertTrue(gitignore_path.exists())
        content = gitignore_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn(".env", content)
        self.assertIn(".sf/", content)
        self.assertIn("__pycache__/", content)
        self.assertIn("node_modules/", content)
        self.assertIn(".spd/", content)
        self.assertIn("session.db*", content)

    def test_preserves_existing_gitignore(self) -> None:
        gitignore_path = self.temp_dir / ".gitignore"
        existing_content = "# Existing custom gitignore\nbuild/\n*.log\n"
        gitignore_path.write_text(existing_content, encoding="utf-8")

        created = ensure_hardened_gitignore(self.temp_dir)
        self.assertFalse(created)
        self.assertEqual(gitignore_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), existing_content)

        scrubbed = git_scrub_tokens(url_with_token)

        # Standalone GitHub tokens

        self.assertNotIn("ghp_111122223333444455556666777788889999", git_scrub_tokens(raw_ghp))

        # Fine-grained PAT
        raw_pat = "github_pat_11AABBCC_secrettokencontent1234567890abcdef"
        self.assertNotIn("secrettokencontent", git_scrub_tokens(raw_pat))
        self.assertIn("github_pat_***", git_scrub_tokens(raw_pat))

class TestRateLimitManager(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test RateLimitManager sliding window and cooldown."""

    def test_sliding_window_accounting(self) -> None:
        rl = RateLimitManager(max_rpm=5)
        status = rl.get_status()
        self.assertFalse(status["cooling_down"])
        self.assertEqual(status["current_rpm"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(status["max_rpm"], 5)

        # Record 3 requests
        rl.record_request()
        rl.record_request()
        rl.record_request()

        status = rl.get_status()
        self.assertEqual(status["current_rpm"], 3)
        self.assertFalse(status["cooling_down"])

    def test_trigger_cooldown(self) -> None:
        rl = RateLimitManager(max_rpm=10)
        rl.trigger_cooldown(duration_s=2.0)

        status = rl.get_status()
        self.assertTrue(status["cooling_down"])
        self.assertGreater(status["cooldown_remaining_s"], 0)

        # Wait out cooldown
        time.sleep(2.1)
        status = rl.get_status()
        self.assertFalse(status["cooling_down"])
        self.assertEqual(status["cooldown_remaining_s"], 0)

    def test_wait_if_needed_cooldown_callback(self) -> None:
        rl = RateLimitManager(max_rpm=10)
        rl.trigger_cooldown(duration_s=0.5)

        callback_invoked = []
        def on_cd(rem: float) -> None:
            callback_invoked.append(rem)

        rl.wait_if_needed(progress_callback=on_cd)
        self.assertTrue(len(callback_invoked) > 0)
        self.assertFalse(rl.get_status()["cooling_down"])


class TestEventSuppression(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test event suppression for self-triggering files."""

    def test_suppress_file_path(self) -> None:

        self.assertTrue(is_path_suppressed("CHANGELOG.md"))
        self.assertTrue(is_path_suppressed("sub/folder/CHANGELOG.md"))
        self.assertFalse(is_path_suppressed("app.py"))

        # Wait for expiration
        time.sleep(1.1)
        self.assertFalse(is_path_suppressed("CHANGELOG.md"))

    def test_event_bundler_drops_suppressed_path(self) -> None:
        bundler = EventBundler(quiet_period=0.5)
        bundler.suppress_path("CHANGELOG.md", duration_s=1.0)

        bundler.add_event("modified", "CHANGELOG.md")
        self.assertEqual(len(bundler._pending_events), 0)

        self.workspace_file = self.temp_dir / "main.py"

        self.assertEqual(reads, ["main.py"])

        # Detect python run
        reads2 = self.tracker._detect_file_reads_from_cmd("python main.py --verbose")
        self.assertEqual(reads2, ["main.py"])

        # Detect non-existent file
        reads3 = self.tracker._detect_file_reads_from_cmd("cat non_existent.txt")
        self.assertEqual(reads3, [])

class MockProc:
    """Mock psutil.Process with name, exe, cmdline, and parents hierarchy."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str = "python.exe",
        exe: str = "C:\\Python\\python.exe",
        cmdline_args: list[str] | None = None,
        parents_list: list[MockProc] | None = None,
        pid: int = 1234,
    ):
        self._name = name
        self._exe = exe
        self._cmdline = cmdline_args or []
        self._parents = parents_list or []
        self.pid = pid
        self.info = {"pid": pid, "name": name}

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def exe(self) -> str:
        return self._exe

    def cmdline(self) -> list[str]:
        return self._cmdline

    def parents(self) -> list[MockProc]:
        return self._parents

    def test_native_vscode_rejection(self) -> None:

            name="Code.exe",
            exe="C:\\Users\\User\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\Code.exe",
            cmdline_args=["Code.exe", "."],
            parents_list=[MockProc("explorer.exe", "C:\\Windows\\explorer.exe")],
        )

class MockProc:
    """Mock process object for psutil tree inspection."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str = "python.exe",
        exe: str = "C:\\Python\\python.exe",
        cmdline_args: list[str] | None = None,
        parents_list: list[MockProc] | None = None,
        pid: int = 1234,
    ):
        self._name = name
        self._exe = exe
        self._cmdline = cmdline_args or []
        self._parents = parents_list or []
        self.pid = pid
        self.info = {"pid": pid, "name": name, "cmdline": self._cmdline}

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def exe(self) -> str:
        return self._exe

    def cmdline(self) -> list[str]:
        return self._cmdline

    def parents(self) -> list[MockProc]:
        return self._parents


class TestAdaptiveFastPolling(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test ExecutionTracker adaptive fast polling rates and debounce triggers."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_test_poll_"))

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_default_intervals(self) -> None:
        tracker = ExecutionTracker(target_dir=self.temp_dir)
        self.assertEqual(tracker.idle_interval, 1.2)
        self.assertEqual(tracker.fast_interval, 0.18)
        self.assertFalse(tracker.is_fast_polling)

    def test_trigger_fast_poll_duration(self) -> None:
        tracker = ExecutionTracker(target_dir=self.temp_dir)
        self.assertFalse(tracker.is_fast_polling)

        tracker.trigger_fast_poll(0.2)
        self.assertTrue(tracker.is_fast_polling)
        time.sleep(0.25)
        self.assertFalse(tracker.is_fast_polling)

    def test_is_active_callback(self) -> None:
        active_state = False
        tracker = ExecutionTracker(
            target_dir=self.temp_dir,
            is_active_callback=lambda: active_state,
        )
        self.assertFalse(tracker.is_fast_polling)
        active_state = True
        self.assertTrue(tracker.is_fast_polling)
        active_state = False
        self.assertFalse(tracker.is_fast_polling)

    def test_event_bundler_activity_accelerates_tracker(self) -> None:
        tracker = ExecutionTracker(target_dir=self.temp_dir)
        self.assertFalse(tracker.is_fast_polling)

        bundler = EventBundler(
            quiet_period=1.0,
            on_activity=lambda: tracker.trigger_fast_poll(0.3),
        )
        # Add event to trigger bundler on_activity
        bundler.add_event("modified", "test.py")
        self.assertTrue(tracker.is_fast_polling)
        bundler.stop()


class TestPowerShellHeadlessFlagDetection(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test PowerShell headless flag detection and AI IDE parent process classification."""

    def test_powershell_and_cmd_headless_flags(self) -> None:
        ai_commands = [
            'powershell -Command "Get-Process"',
            'powershell.exe -command "Get-Service"',
            'pwsh -Command "dir"',
            'pwsh.exe -c "ls"',
            'powershell -encodedcommand VwByAGkAdABlAC0ASABvAHMAdAA=',
            'powershell.exe -file ./build.ps1',
            'pwsh -file scripts/deploy.ps1',
            'cmd.exe /c dir',
            '/c echo test',
            'cmd.exe /c "npm run test"',
        ]
        for cmd in ai_commands:
            self.assertEqual(
                detect_executor(cmd),
                "AI_AGENT",
                f"Expected AI_AGENT for command: {cmd}",
            )

    def test_human_interactive_commands(self) -> None:
        human_commands = [
            'git status',
            'git commit -m "feat: implement feature"',
            'git diff HEAD~1',
            'npm test',
            'npm run build',
            'python main.py',
            'dir',
            'pytest tests/',
        ]
        for cmd in human_commands:
            self.assertEqual(
                detect_executor(cmd),
                "HUMAN_DEV",
                f"Expected HUMAN_DEV for command: {cmd}",
            )

    def test_ai_ide_parent_classification(self) -> None:
        """Commands executed under an Antigravity parent process must be classified as AI_AGENT."""
        antigravity_parent = MockProc(
            name="antigravity.exe",
            exe="C:\\Users\\User\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Antigravity\\antigravity.exe",
            cmdline_args=["antigravity.exe"],
        )
        child_cmd_proc = MockProc(
            name="powershell.exe",
            exe="C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe",
            cmdline_args=["powershell.exe"],
            parents_list=[antigravity_parent],
        )

        # Even with interactive command text, parent process tree marks it as AI_AGENT
        res = detect_executor("git status", proc=child_cmd_proc, ide_profile="antigravity")
        self.assertEqual(res, "AI_AGENT")

        res_npm = detect_executor("npm test", proc=child_cmd_proc, ide_profile="antigravity")
        self.assertEqual(res_npm, "AI_AGENT")


class TestAISynthesizerExplainCommand(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test AISynthesizer explain_command and heuristic fallback."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_test_ai_"))
        self.syn = AISynthesizer(engine_root=self.temp_dir)

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_heuristic_fallback_git_status(self) -> None:
        result = self.syn._fallback_command_explanation(
            command_str="git status",
            exit_code=0,
            duration_s=0.15,
        )
        self.assertIn("intent", result)
        self.assertIn("technical_purpose", result)
        self.assertIn("outcome_analysis", result)
        self.assertIn("summary", result)
        self.assertIn("Inspect", result["intent"])
        self.assertIn("exit code 0", result["outcome_analysis"])
        self.assertTrue(len(result["summary"]) >= 1)

    def test_heuristic_fallback_failure_exit(self) -> None:
        result = self.syn._fallback_command_explanation(
            command_str="pytest",
            exit_code=1,
            duration_s=1.45,
        )
        self.assertIn("non-zero", result["outcome_analysis"])
        self.assertIn("exit code 1", result["outcome_analysis"])

    def test_explain_command_heuristic_mode(self) -> None:
        res = self.syn.explain_command(
            project_name="test_proj",
            command_str="python -c 'import sys; print(sys.version)'",
            exit_code=0,
            duration_s=0.12,
            provider="heuristic",
        )
        self.assertEqual(res["provider"], "heuristic")
        self.assertIn("Python", res["intent"])
        self.assertIn("technical_purpose", res)
        self.assertIn("outcome_analysis", res)

        # Test caching on second call
        res_cached = self.syn.explain_command(
            project_name="test_proj",
            command_str="python -c 'import sys; print(sys.version)'",
            exit_code=0,
            duration_s=0.12,
            provider="heuristic",
        )
        self.assertEqual(res_cached["diff_hash"], res["diff_hash"])

"""
tests/test_v9_crash_rollback_and_lap.py
=======================================
Unit tests for Crash & Ungraceful Termination Sentinel, Granular Burst Rollback,
Manual Burst Sealing (Lap Button), Debounce Window expansion, and Native .git
Remote Auto-Discovery in the SPD Analysis Engine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from scripts.event_bundler import EventBundler
from scripts.git_shadow import ShadowGit, discover_native_git_remote

class TestEventBundlerLapSealing(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test EventBundler.flush_burst_now() immediate manual sealing."""

    def test_flush_burst_now_emits_pending_bundle(self) -> None:
        emitted_bundles: list[dict] = []

        def on_bundle(b: dict) -> None:
            emitted_bundles.append(b)

        bundler = EventBundler(
            callback=on_bundle,
            quiet_period=30.0,  # Long quiet period so timer does not fire naturally
        )

        # Initially idle
        self.assertFalse(bundler.is_pending)
        self.assertIsNone(bundler.flush_burst_now())

        # Add events
        bundler.add_event("modified", "src/index.js")
        bundler.add_event("created", "src/utils.js")

        self.assertTrue(bundler.is_pending)
        status = bundler.get_debounce_status()
        self.assertTrue(status["active"])
        self.assertEqual(status["files_count"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(status["first_file"], "src/index.js")

        # Manually seal burst (Lap Button)
        bundle = bundler.flush_burst_now()
        self.assertIsNotNone(bundle)
        assert bundle is not None
        self.assertEqual(len(bundle["files_touched"]), 2)
        self.assertEqual(bundle["first_file"], "src/index.js")
        self.assertEqual(len(emitted_bundles), 1)

        # State should be reset to idle
        self.assertFalse(bundler.is_pending)
        status_after = bundler.get_debounce_status()
        self.assertFalse(status_after["active"])

        # Second flush returns None since queue was cleared
        self.assertIsNone(bundler.flush_burst_now())
        bundler.stop()


class TestNativeGitRemoteAutoDiscovery(unittest.TestCase):

        self.assertEqual(branch, "")

    def test_discover_git_repo_with_remote(self) -> None:
        if not self.git_available:
            self.skipTest("git binary not available on host system")

        repo_dir = self.temp_dir / "my_repo"
        repo_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Initialize git repo and add mock origin
        subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=str(repo_dir), check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", "https://github.com/myorg/awesome-app.git"],
            cwd=str(repo_dir),
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
        )

        remote_url, branch = discover_native_git_remote(repo_dir)
        self.assertEqual(remote_url, "https://github.com/myorg/awesome-app.git")
        self.assertIn(branch, ["main", "master"])

    def test_read_project_meta_auto_discovers_remote(self) -> None:
        if not self.git_available:
            self.skipTest("git binary not available on host system")

        engine_root = self.temp_dir / "engine"
        repo_dir = self.temp_dir / "target_repo"
        repo_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=str(repo_dir), check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", "git@github.com:test/repo.git"],
            cwd=str(repo_dir),
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
        )

        rotator = StorageRotator(engine_root)
        proj_dir = rotator.init_project("test_auto_remote", str(repo_dir))

        meta = read_project_meta(engine_root, "test_auto_remote")
        self.assertEqual(meta.get("remote_url"), "git@github.com:test/repo.git")
        self.assertEqual(meta.get("clean_exit"), "false")
        self.assertEqual(meta.get("status"), "active")

        # Simulate worker creating session.lock

class TestGranularBurstRollback(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test rollback_burst() removing events from DB, rolling back shadow git, and moving to trash."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spd_rollback_test_"))
        self.engine_root = self.temp_dir / "engine"
        self.engine_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.target_dir = self.temp_dir / "target"
        self.target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        self.rotator = StorageRotator(self.engine_root)
        self.proj_dir = self.rotator.init_project("rollback_demo", str(self.target_dir))
        self.db_path = self.proj_dir / "session.db"
        self.db = SessionDB(self.db_path)
        self.sid = self.db.create_session("rollback_demo", str(self.target_dir))

        self.server = EngineWebServer(engine_root=self.engine_root, port=0)

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.db.close()
        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_rollback_burst_and_move_to_trash(self) -> None:
        # Create an event in DB
        ev_id = self.db.record_event(
            session_id=self.sid,
            event_type="EDIT",
            first_file="main.py",
            summary="Prompt Burst #1: Modified 1 file(s)",
        )
        self.db.record_patch(
            event_id=ev_id,
            file_path="main.py",
            diff_content="--- a/main.py\n+++ b/main.py\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-old\n+new",
        )

        # Create patch file on disk
        patches_dir = self.proj_dir / "patches"
        patches_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        patch_file = patches_dir / f"event_{ev_id}.patch"
        patch_file.write_text("patch content", encoding="utf-8")

        # Also create associated GIT micro-commit event
        git_ev_id = self.db.record_event(
            session_id=self.sid,
            event_type="GIT",
            first_file=None,
            summary=f"Micro-commit: Burst #{ev_id}: Modified 1 file(s)",
        )

        # Perform rollback
        res = rollback_burst(self.engine_root, "rollback_demo", ev_id)
        self.assertTrue(res.get("success"))
        self.assertEqual(res.get("event_id"), ev_id)

        # Verify event and git event are removed from session.db
        cur = self.db.conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM events WHERE id = ?", (ev_id,))
        self.assertIsNone(cur.fetchone())
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM events WHERE id = ?", (git_ev_id,))
        self.assertIsNone(cur.fetchone())

        # Verify patch rows are deleted
        cur.execute("SELECT id FROM patches WHERE event_id = ?", (ev_id,))
        self.assertEqual(len(cur.fetchall()), 0)

        # Verify moved to trash under selective_bursts
        tm = TrashManager(self.engine_root)
        trash_items = tm.list_trash()
        burst_trash = next((item for item in trash_items if item["scope"] == SCOPE_SELECTIVE_BURSTS), None)
        self.assertIsNotNone(burst_trash)
        assert burst_trash is not None
        self.assertEqual(burst_trash["project_name"], "rollback_demo")
        details = burst_trash.get("details") or burst_trash.get("metadata") or {}
        self.assertIn(ev_id, details.get("burst_ids", []))

    def test_web_server_rollback_endpoint(self) -> None:
        ev_id = self.db.record_event(
            session_id=self.sid,
            event_type="EDIT",
            first_file="config.py",
            summary="Prompt Burst #2: Modified 1 file(s)",
        )

def test_web_server() -> int:
    print("\n" + "=" * 65)
    print("  PHASE 3 VERIFICATION: EngineWebServer & Control Portal API")
    print("=" * 65 + "\n")

    port = 8799
    server = EngineWebServer(engine_root=_ENGINE_ROOT, port=port)
    actual_port = server.start(background=True)
    base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{actual_port}"
    print(f"[1/7] EngineWebServer started at {base_url}")

    failures: list[str] = []

    try:
        # 1. Test Static Assets
        print("\n[2/7] Testing static asset serving...")
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"{base_url}/")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            content = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
            assert resp.status == 200
            assert "SPD Engine" in content
            print("      [PASS] GET / returned index.html (200 OK)")

        req_css = urllib.request.Request(f"{base_url}/style.css")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_css) as resp:
            assert resp.status == 200
            assert "var(--bg-app)" in resp.read().decode("utf-8")
            print("      [PASS] GET /style.css returned stylesheet (200 OK)")

        req_js = urllib.request.Request(f"{base_url}/app.js")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_js) as resp:
            assert resp.status == 200
            assert "refreshProjects" in resp.read().decode("utf-8")
            print("      [PASS] GET /app.js returned client JS (200 OK)")

        # 2. Test GET /api/status & GET /api/projects
        print("\n[3/7] Testing /api/status and /api/projects...")
        req_status = urllib.request.Request(f"{base_url}/api/status")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_status) as resp:
            data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            assert data["status"] == "ok"
            assert "workers" in data
            print(f"      [PASS] GET /api/status returned {len(data['workers'])} worker(s)")

        req_projects = urllib.request.Request(f"{base_url}/api/projects")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_projects) as resp:
            proj_data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            assert "current" in proj_data
            assert "last_run" in proj_data
            assert "history" in proj_data
            print(f"      [PASS] GET /api/projects returned grouped tiers (current: {len(proj_data['current'])}, last_run: {len(proj_data['last_run'])})")

        # 3. Test POST /api/projects/start
        test_proj = "web_portal_test"
        test_ws = _ENGINE_ROOT / "mock_workspace" / test_proj
        if test_ws.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(test_ws, ignore_errors=True)

        print(f"\n[4/7] Testing POST /api/projects/start for '{test_proj}'...")
        start_payload = {
            "project": test_proj,
            "path": str(test_ws),
            "scaffold": True,
            "debounce": 1.5,
        }
        start_req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{base_url}/api/projects/start",
            data=json.dumps(start_payload).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(start_req) as resp:
            start_res = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            assert start_res["status"] == "started"
            worker_pid = start_res["result"]["pid"]
            print(f"      [PASS] Worker started successfully | PID={worker_pid}")

        # Wait for worker boot
        time.sleep(2.0)

        # 4. Verify worker in /api/status and /api/project/<name>/logs
        print("\n[5/7] Verifying live worker and logs...")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/api/status") as resp:
            live_status = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            alive_match = [w for w in live_status["workers"] if w["project"] == test_proj and w["alive"]]
            if not alive_match:
                failures.append(f"Worker '{test_proj}' not reported alive in /api/status")
                print(f"      [FAIL] {failures[-1]}")
            else:
                print(f"      [PASS] Worker '{test_proj}' is LIVE (PID {alive_match[0]['pid']})")

        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/api/project/{test_proj}/logs") as resp:
            logs_res = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            assert "lines" in logs_res
            print(f"      [PASS] /api/project/{test_proj}/logs returned {len(logs_res['lines'])} lines")

        # 5. Simulate file change and verify /api/project/<name>/events
        print("\n[6/7] Simulating file modification and testing events/export API...")
        sample_file = test_ws / "index.py"
        sample_file.write_text("def run():\n    return 'Hello from Web Portal Test'\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"      Wrote file: {sample_file}")

        # Wait for debounce (1.5s quiet window + 1.0s buffer)
        print("      Waiting 2.5s for 1.5s debounce timer to fire...")
        time.sleep(2.5)

        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/api/project/{test_proj}/events") as resp:
            events_res = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            ev_list = events_res.get("events", [])
            print(f"      Events retrieved: {len(ev_list)}")
            if len(ev_list) == 0:
                failures.append("No events recorded for file modification")
                print(f"      [FAIL] {failures[-1]}")
            else:
                ev = ev_list[0]
                print(f"      [PASS] Recorded Event #{ev['id']}: {ev['summary']}")
                patches = ev.get("patches", [])
                if patches:
                    print(f"      [PASS] Found {len(patches)} patch(es) for {patches[0]['file_path']}")
                else:
                    failures.append("Event missing patches")
                    print(f"      [FAIL] {failures[-1]}")

        # Export endpoint test
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/api/project/{test_proj}/export") as resp:
            export_data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            assert export_data["project"] == test_proj
            assert "events" in export_data
            print(f"      [PASS] GET /api/project/{test_proj}/export returned valid bundle ({len(export_data['events'])} events)")

        # 6. Test POST /api/projects/stop
        print(f"\n[7/7] Testing POST /api/projects/stop for '{test_proj}'...")
        stop_payload = {"project": test_proj}
        stop_req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{base_url}/api/projects/stop",
            data=json.dumps(stop_payload).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(stop_req) as resp:
            stop_res = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            assert stop_res["status"] == "stopped"
            print(f"      [PASS] Project '{test_proj}' stopped and archived successfully")

    except Exception as exc:
        failures.append(f"Unexpected exception: {exc}")
        print(f"[ERROR] {exc}")
    finally:
        # Clean shutdown of server
        server.shutdown()
        # Clean up test mock workspace
        shutil.rmtree(_ENGINE_ROOT / "mock_workspace" / "web_portal_test", ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.rmtree(_ENGINE_ROOT / "last_run" / "web_portal_test", ignore_errors=True)

    print("\n" + "=" * 65)
    if not failures:
        print("  >>> ALL PHASE 3 WEB SERVER TESTS PASSED (100% SUCCESS) <<<")
        print("=" * 65 + "\n")
        return 0
    else:
        print(f"  >>> FAILED WITH {len(failures)} ERROR(S) <<<")
        for f in failures:
            print(f"   - {f}")
        print("=" * 65 + "\n")
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(test_web_server())

/**
 * SPD Analysis Engine — Web Control Portal Client Coordinator
 * Pure Vanilla JavaScript (Zero external framework/CDN dependencies)
 */
import { state } from './js/state.js';
import { DOM } from './js/dom.js';
import { initSSE } from './js/stream.js';
import { refreshProjects, loadProjectLogs, initDashboardListeners } from './js/views/dashboard.js';
import { loadProjectEvents, initTimelineListeners, setTimelineNavigationHooks } from './js/views/timeline.js';
import { initDiffListeners } from './js/views/diff_viewer.js';
import { updateTrashCount, initModalListeners } from './js/views/modals.js';
import { setupSidebarToggle, switchView } from './js/sidebar.js';
import { initEcoMode } from './js/eco_mode.js';

export function selectTab(tabName) {
  state.activeTab = tabName;
  switchView(tabName);

  try {
    if ((tabName === 'timeline' || tabName === 'diffs' || tabName === 'diff' || tabName === 'terminal') && state.selectedProject) {
      loadProjectEvents(state.selectedProject);
    } else if (tabName === 'logs' && state.selectedProject) {
      loadProjectLogs(state.selectedProject);
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`Error activating tab '${tabName}':`, err);
  }
}

export { switchView };

// Expose global window hooks for atomic view switching and view data refresh
window.switchView = selectTab;
window.selectTab = selectTab;
window.refreshDiffView = () => {
  if (state.selectedProject) {
    loadProjectEvents(state.selectedProject);
  }
};
window.refreshWorkerLogs = () => {
  if (state.selectedProject) {
    loadProjectLogs(state.selectedProject);
  }
};

async function init() {
  try {
    setTimelineNavigationHooks({
      onSelectTab: selectTab,
      onRefreshProjects: refreshProjects,
      onUpdateTrashCount: updateTrashCount,
      onRenderDashboardRecentEvents: (events) => {
        import('./js/views/dashboard.js')
          .then((m) => m.renderDashboardRecentEvents(events))
          .catch((err) => console.warn('Render recent events error:', err));
      },
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error setting timeline navigation hooks:', err);
  }

  try {
    setupSidebarToggle();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing sidebar toggle:', err);
  }

  try {
    initDashboardListeners();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing dashboard listeners:', err);
  }

  try {
    initTimelineListeners();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing timeline listeners:', err);
  }

  try {
    initDiffListeners();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing diff listeners:', err);
  }

  try {
    initModalListeners();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing modal listeners:', err);
  }

  try {
    initEcoMode();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing eco mode:', err);
  }

  try {
    if (DOM.navButtons) {
      DOM.navButtons.forEach((btn) => {
        btn.addEventListener('click', () => selectTab(btn.dataset.view || btn.dataset.tab));
      });
    }

    if (DOM.btnViewAllTimeline) {
      DOM.btnViewAllTimeline.addEventListener('click', () => selectTab('timeline'));
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error binding navigation button listeners:', err);
  }

  try {
    await updateTrashCount();
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('Initial trash count update error:', err);
  }

  try {
    await refreshProjects();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Initial refresh projects error:', err);
  }

  try {
    initSSE();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Error initializing SSE connection:', err);
  }
}

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);

#debounce-progress-bar {
  width: 100%;
  height: 8px;
  background-color: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.8);
  border-radius: 9999px;
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
  transition: width 1.0s linear;
  will-change: width;
}

.debounce-progress-fill,
#debounce-progress-fill {
  height: 100%;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, #38bdf8, #818cf8, #a855f7);
  background-size: 200% 100%;
  border-radius: 9999px;
  transition: width 1.0s linear;
  will-change: width;
}

.debounce-progress-fill.active {
  animation: progressStripes 1.5s linear infinite;
}

@keyframes progressStripes {
  0% { background-position: 100% 0; }
  100% { background-position: 0 0; }
}

.debounce-progress-labels {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  color: var(--text-muted);
}

.slider-presets-row {
  display: flex;
  gap: 6px;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  margin-top: 6px;
}

.slider-presets-row .btn-debounce-preset {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-subtle);
  color: var(--text-muted);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  padding: 3px 8px;
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: all 0.15s ease;
}

.slider-presets-row .btn-debounce-preset:hover,
.slider-presets-row .btn-debounce-preset.active {
  background: rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.15);
  border-color: var(--accent-blue);
  color: #ffffff;
}

/* ==========================================================================
   LIVE ACTIVITY STREAM TICKER CARD
   ========================================================================== */

.live-ticker-card {
  border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.25);
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(30, 41, 59, 0.5) 0%, rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.7) 100%);
  margin-bottom: 20px;
}

.live-dot-pulse {
  width: 9px;
  height: 9px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background-color: #3b82f6;
  box-shadow: 0 0 8px #3b82f6;
  display: inline-block;
  animation: pulse-ticker 1.6s infinite;
}

@keyframes pulse-ticker {
  0% { transform: scale(0.9); opacity: 0.7; }
  50% { transform: scale(1.3); opacity: 1; box-shadow: 0 0 12px #60a5fa; }
  100% { transform: scale(0.9); opacity: 0.7; }
}

.live-ticker-feed {
  min-height: 220px;
  max-height: 320px;
  overflow-y: auto;
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  line-height: 1.6;
  padding: 12px 14px;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 6px;
  background-color: rgba(10, 15, 28, 0.85);
  border-radius: 8px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.2);
}

.ticker-row {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 3px 6px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  transition: background-color 0.1s ease;
}

.ticker-row:hover {
  background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);
}

.ticker-ts {
  color: var(--text-dim);
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

.ticker-badge {
  font-size: 0.68rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  padding: 1px 6px;
  border-radius: 3px;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

.ticker-badge.write { background-color: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.18); color: #10b981; border: 1px solid rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.4); }
.ticker-badge.read  { background-color: rgba(14, 165, 233, 0.18); color: #0ea5e9; border: 1px solid rgba(14, 165, 233, 0.4); }
.ticker-badge.exec  { background-color: rgba(168, 85, 247, 0.18); color: #a855f7; border: 1px solid rgba(168, 85, 247, 0.4); }
.ticker-badge.burst { background-color: rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.2); color: #4ade80; border: 1px solid rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.4); }

.ticker-file {
  color: var(--text-main);
  word-break: break-all;
}

.ticker-details {
  color: var(--text-muted);
  font-size: 0.74rem;
  margin-left: auto;
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

.ticker-empty {
  color: var(--text-dim);
  font-style: italic;
  padding: 12px;
  text-align: center;
}

/* ==========================================================================
   PROJECT CONFIGURATION & SPECS CARD
   ========================================================================== */

.project-specs-card {
  border: 1px solid rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.25);
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(30, 41, 59, 0.45) 0%, rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.65) 100%);
  margin-bottom: 20px;
}

.specs-header-title {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
}

.specs-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr));
  gap: 16px 24px;
}

.spec-item {

}

.spec-label {
  font-size: 0.72rem;

.spec-value {

}

.spec-value.mono {

}

.specs-checklist {

}

.spec-check-pill {
  font-size: 0.70rem;

}

.spec-check-pill.active {
  background: rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.15);

  border-color: rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.35);
}

.spec-remote-row {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 10px;
}

/* ==========================================================================
   TIMELINE, READS, TERMINAL & AI CARDS
   ========================================================================== */

.timeline-container {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 14px;
}

.timeline-card {

/* AI Intent & Functional Gains Card — Neutral Slate-Grey Surface */

/* Worker Logs Terminal */

}

.ai-progress-track {

/* ==========================================================================
   SPD Analysis Engine — GPU Optimization ("Eco Mode")
   Eliminates backdrop filters, glows, shadows, and infinite decorative loops
   while ensuring all cards, views, and containers remain fully visible.
   ========================================================================== */

body.eco-mode,
.eco-mode {
  --bg-primary: #13151b;
  --bg-secondary: #141721;
  --bg-card: #141721;
  --bg-card-hover: #1c202d;
  --bg-app: #13151b;
  --bg-sidebar: #141721;
  --bg-header: #141721;
  --bg-surface-2: #141721;
  --border-color: #232738;
  --border-card: #232738;
  --accent-glow: transparent;
  background-color: #13151b !important;
}

body.eco-mode *,
.eco-mode * {
  backdrop-filter: none !important;
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: none !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  text-shadow: none !important;
}

/* Instantaneous transitions to eliminate rendering overhead */
.eco-mode * {
  transition-duration: 0.05s !important;
}

/* Only apply solid backgrounds and disable blurs on ACTIVE views */
.eco-mode .view-pane.active,
.eco-mode .tab-view.active {
  background: #0d1117 !important;
  opacity: 1 !important;
  display: flex !important;
}

/* Guarantee non-active panes remain completely hidden in Eco Mode */
.eco-mode .view-pane:not(.active),
.eco-mode .tab-view:not(.active) {
  display: none !important;
  visibility: hidden !important;
  opacity: 0 !important;
  height: 0 !important;
}

/* Force all active cards and containers to remain fully visible */
.eco-mode .card,
.eco-mode .dashboard-grid,
.eco-mode .spec-card,
.eco-mode .project-tier-group,
.eco-mode .header,
.eco-mode .sidebar,
.eco-mode .metric-card,
.eco-mode .modal-box,
.eco-mode .modal-content,
.eco-mode .tray-body,
.eco-mode .global-job-tray,
.eco-mode .timeline-card,
.eco-mode .diff-step-card,
.eco-mode .diff-sidebar,
.eco-mode .diff-code-panel,
.eco-mode .diff-viewer-main,
.eco-mode .live-ticker-feed,
.eco-mode .live-ticker-card,
.eco-mode .ai-analysis-card,
.eco-mode .heuristic-notice-card,
.eco-mode .git-test-card,
.eco-mode .preflight-card,
.eco-mode .settings-tab-pane:not(.hidden),
.eco-mode .health-card,
.eco-mode .settings-section-card {
  opacity: 1 !important;
  transform: none !important;
  background: #141721 !important;
  border: 1px solid #232738 !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  backdrop-filter: none !important;
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: none !important;
}

/* Target ONLY infinite decorative loops to eliminate background GPU rasterization */
.eco-mode .pulse-ring,
.eco-mode .pulse-dot,
.eco-mode .sse-live-indicator,
.eco-mode .spinner,
.eco-mode .btn-spinner,
.eco-mode .tray-spinner {
  animation: none !important;
  animation-play-state: paused !important;
}

.eco-mode .modal-backdrop {
  background-color: rgba(10, 12, 16, 0.88) !important;
  backdrop-filter: none !important;
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: none !important;
}

/* Style for the Eco Mode toggle button in active state */
.btn-eco-mode.active,
#btn-header-eco-mode.active {
  background: #22c55e !important;
  color: #0b0f19 !important;
  font-weight: 700 !important;
  border-color: #16a34a !important;
}

.view-container {

/* All view panes are strictly hidden by default */
.view-pane,
.tab-view {
  display: none !important;
  visibility: hidden !important;
  opacity: 0;
  height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
}

/* Only the active pane is rendered and takes layout space */
.view-pane.active,
.tab-view.active {
  display: flex !important;
  flex-direction: column;
  visibility: visible !important;
  opacity: 1 !important;
  height: auto !important;
  min-height: calc(100vh - 72px);

  animation: fadeIn 0.15s ease-in-out;

.view-header-bar {

  }
}

/* ==========================================================================
   Circular Button Loading Spinner
   ========================================================================== */
.spinner-icon {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 13px;
  height: 13px;
  border: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35);
  border-top-color: currentColor;
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spd-spin 0.75s linear infinite;
  vertical-align: middle;
  margin-right: 6px;
}

@keyframes spd-spin {
  to {
    transform: rotate(360deg);
  }
}

.btn-loading {
  opacity: 0.85;
  cursor: not-allowed !important;
  pointer-events: none;
}

  z-index: 250;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  overflow: hidden;
  animation: slideInUp 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
  backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
}

@keyframes slideInUp {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px); }
  to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
}

.tray-header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 10px 14px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-card);
}

.tray-title-area {
  display: flex;

  gap: 8px;
}

.tray-spinner {
  width: 14px;
  height: 14px;
  border: 2px solid rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.3);
  border-top-color: var(--accent-purple);
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spin 0.8s linear infinite;
  display: inline-block;
}

.tray-title {
  font-size: 0.82rem;

}

.tray-close-btn {

}

.tray-close-btn:hover {

}

.tray-body {
  padding: 12px 14px;

}

.tray-project {

  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.tray-progress-wrap {
  width: 100%;
  height: 6px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
  border-radius: 3px;
  overflow: hidden;
}

.tray-progress-bar {
  height: 100%;

}

.tray-stats-row {

}

.tray-percent {

}

.tray-cooldown-badge {

#btn-header-push-git {

/* GitHub Push 3-Step Progress Stepper */

.sync-stepper-container {
